verdict_reason: The paper's own descriptor is now computed, and computed exactly. I ran the authors' post_process.py (RitAreaSciencePark/ZigZagLLMs) and BLME's _betti/span side by side on the barcode they ship, llama_3_8b_dim_4_knn_4_last_token.csv: identical beta_1 vectors (14176, 15828, 17260, ..., 16321) and identical inter-layer persistence rows Z_1(l,l+1) = (0.092551, 0.201542, ..., 0.433460), max absolute difference 0.0 on both, including Z_1(0,32) = 0.0. I re-derived Eq. 7 from the paper text -- numerator sum over PI_hat with birth <= min(l1,l2) and death > max(l1,l2), denominator beta_p(l1) -- and the code's denominator choice is the paper's, not the total bar count. I also verified the construction is the paper's INTERSECTION zigzag rather than the union: on a hexagon 0-5 with centre 6 carrying spokes {6-0,6-1,6-2} in layer A and {6-3,6-4,6-5} in layer B, the dionysus time convention BLME builds returns one H1 bar spanning both layers (union would give 0). dionysus 2.1.1 is now a hard dependency and is present, so the metric is no longer silently absent in production.
comparable_reason: The reported quantities are ratios to each layer's own beta_1 and are bounded in [0,1], which is the right form: measured zz_true_adjacent_mean = 0.1630 (pythia-70m, 6 layers, d=512), 0.3190 (pythia-160m, 12 layers, d=768), 0.3559 (distilgpt2, 6 layers, d=768), 0.4741 (gpt2, 12 layers, d=768) -- no monotone relation to depth or width in that set. The caveat is that the DENOMINATOR, the cycle rank of a kNN flag complex, grows with the point count, so the ratio is only comparable at a fixed num_samples; the raw counts are correctly demoted to _meta_. This task is absent from the 66-model snapshot, so there is no zoo-scale correlation to report.
normalized_variant: zz_h1_survival_rate / zz_h1_turnover_rate (GF(2) fallback family); zz_true_adjacent_mean (dionysus family)
github_reason: Ran the authors' own src/plots/post_process.py (POSTPROCESS with num_layers=66, start_ind=1, zigzag=True) on the barcode CSV shipped in their repo and compared its find_betti_layers() and find_ph_sim()/betti outputs against BLME's _betti and span on the same bars: max absolute difference 0.0 for the whole 33-entry beta_1 vector and the whole 32-entry Z_1(l,l+1) row. Their effective-persistence-image mapping (eff = i//2 + i%2, drop eff_b == eff_d) is exactly BLME's [a, b+1) time convention. Also confirmed from their code that a Z_p(l,l) == 1 self-check is tautological in the reference too -- psim[idx,idx] is literally the sum that defines beta(idx) -- so removing BLME's _meta_zz_true_identity_ok removed a check that could not fail.
paper_reason: The paper (ICML 2025, arXiv:2410.11042) publishes figures, not tables, so there is no printed scalar to hit. The strongest available check is against the artefact they released, and it is exact (see github_reason). The paper's stated magnitude claim is also reproduced: '1-dimensional holes reach tens of thousands of elements per layer' -- BLME's beta_1 read of their barcode gives 14,176 to 18,658 per layer.
confounds_reason: The reported quantities are dimensionless ratios of H1 classes to H1 classes within the same model, and across the four models I ran they do not order by depth (6-layer distilgpt2 0.3559 > 12-layer pythia-160m 0.3190) or by width (pythia-70m at d=512 is lowest, but pythia-160m and gpt2 share d=768 and differ 0.319 vs 0.474). The scale-dependent raw counts (_meta_zz_h1_dim_mean 4.7 to 9.8 here) are already _meta_-prefixed and excluded from the feature matrix.
defects: 10 to 11 of the ~15 non-meta exported keys are identically zero on every model I ran. Measured on gpt2, distilgpt2, pythia-70m and pythia-160m at the shipped config: h1_total_layer_persistence, h1_loop_layer_sum, h1_num_bands, h1_max_band_length, h1_first_layer, h1_last_layer, betti1_fraction_layers, h0_persistence_range and zz_true_full_depth are all 0.0, plus zz_true_adjacent_min on three of the four. The legacy band family is dead because it still uses the weighted-geodesic construction with persistence_frac = 0.3, the exact unreachable threshold that topology_betti_curve was just fixed to abandon -- and it is dead while the true family is alive on the same data (distilgpt2 beta_1 per layer = [9, 8, 15, 7, 12, 1]).

zz_true_full_depth is zero for the AUTHORS' own barcode too (Z_1(0,32) = 0.0 on llama_3_8b), so it is not a BLME artefact -- but it is a constant-zero feature and should not be shipped as a predictor.

DUPLICATE: zz_h1_survival_rate is numerically identical to zz_true_adjacent_mean whenever dionysus is present -- 0.474069364978456 vs 0.474069364978456 on gpt2, and identical to full precision on all four models. That is a useful cross-validation of the GF(2) fallback against the dionysus barcode, but they must not both enter the feature matrix.

CODE (latent deviation from the paper's own text): the paper's footnote to Eq. 7 states that when there are no p-dimensional holes at either layer, Z_p 'should be 0 by definition'. BLME returns NaN when beta_p(l1) = 0 and then DROPS that step from the mean, which inflates the reported average. It did not fire on any of the four models (beta_1 >= 1 at every layer of every model, _meta_zz_n_steps = n_layers - 1 in all cases), so no shipped number is affected today -- but a shallow or degenerate cloud would make BLME's mean differ from the paper's, and NaN also breaks json.dumps(allow_nan=False).

CODE (documentation): the module docstring (lines 34-50) is stale and now false. It still says 'BLME cannot depend on dionysus/fzz (C++ builds that are not repo deps and fail against modern Boost)' -- dionysus==2.1.1 is now a required dependency and is what computes the metric -- and it still claims the band summary 'reproduces, by construction, the exact dionysus zigzag answer', a claim the code's own newer comment retracts.

CONFIG: num_samples = 40 against the paper's 500-prompt subsets drawn from 8,000 prompts; their barcodes carry ~15,000 H1 classes per layer, BLME's _meta_zz_h1_dim_mean is 4.7 to 9.8. The ratio form absorbs some of this but the estimator is noisy at 40 points.
CONFIG: n_neighbors = 5 matches the arXiv v1 and the repo README, but the ICML camera-ready reports results 'for k_NN = 4 only'. Not wrong, but the shipped value tracks the superseded version.
DISCLOSED: BLME mean-pools tokens per prompt where Gardinazzi et al. take the last token at each normalisation layer. This changes the point cloud, not the zigzag construction.
fix: 1) Stop exporting the nine-to-eleven constant keys as first-class features: either delete the legacy band family (its persistence_frac = 0.3 threshold on a weighted geodesic is unreachable, exactly as it was in topology_betti_curve before that task was fixed) or _meta_-prefix it, and drop zz_true_full_depth, which is zero for the authors' own data. 2) Demote one of zz_h1_survival_rate / zz_true_adjacent_mean -- they are the same number to 16 digits whenever dionysus is installed. 3) Follow the paper's footnote and return 0.0, not NaN, when beta_p(l1) = 0, so the mean matches the reference convention and the output is JSON-safe. 4) Rewrite the stale module docstring: dionysus is now required, the band summary is a presence proxy, and the identity self-check was removed as tautological. 5) Consider raising num_samples toward the paper's 500 and adding the paper's Z_p(l, l_i) profile over all target layers, of which the adjacent mean is one slice. Do NOT revert the codex RED on this task: I reproduced its counterexample (A = square1, B = square1+square2, C = square1 vs square2) and the current code distinguishes the two sequences correctly -- zz_true_full_depth = 1.0 vs 0.0 -- because the dionysus barcode, not the pairwise GF(2) family, is what is reported.
